regions.label: Figure 7.2
regions.summary: Treemap comparison of antitrust cases involving digital platforms by sector in high-income and middle-income countries. Passenger transport accounts for a much larger share in middle-income countries (35%) than in high-income countries (8%).
regions.details: Title: “In the digital economy, antitrust cases related to passenger transport are more prevalent in middle-income countries than in high-income countries.” Two treemap panels show percentages of cases by sector. Panel a, high-income countries: Retail e-commerce 21%; Others 15%; Online search and advertising 15%; Software and operating systems 15%; Tourism (accommodation) 13%; Social media and communications 10%; Passenger transport 8%; Online real estate platforms 5%. Panel b, middle-income countries: Passenger transport 35%; Retail e-commerce 23%; Software and operating systems 18%; Others 10%; Mobile financial services 8%; Online search and advertising 8%. Note states cases total 62 in high-income countries and 40 in middle-income countries; percentages are based on publicly available information as of January 2020. Panel a “Others” includes digital music, e-books, educational materials, food delivery, online comparison platforms, dating platforms, and ticketing. Panel b “Others” includes online delivery services, ticketing, and tourism. Source: Nyman and Barajas, forthcoming; data URL printed as http://bit.do/WDR2021-Fig-7_2. Note says no cases were finalized in low-income countries according to publicly available information.
regions.limitations: Treemap areas and labels are visible; percentages are printed as whole numbers, so totals may differ from 100 because of rounding. No values are shown for sectors omitted from the middle-income panel.
